workbench.lead: Tools for working with the data yourself. Everything runs in your browser: there is no server, no account, and nothing you load leaves your device.
workbench.desc.sql: Query the published Parquet files with SQL, or build a query visually and see the SQL it generates.
workbench.desc.notebooks: Python and R notebooks that reproduce the site’s charts and flags, in the browser or as downloads.
workbench.desc.pivot: Sort, group and cross-tabulate a disease’s data, with a linked chart.
workbench.desc.chart-builder: Choose variables and a chart type, then export the image and its specification.
workbench.desc.linked: Brush a date range or pick countries, and the map, table and event list follow.
workbench.desc.diff: See which values changed between two snapshots, by how much, and from which source.
workbench.desc.map-select: Draw a region or pick countries, then compare two groups.
workbench.desc.overlay: Plot your own CSV next to the official data. It stays on your device.
workbench.privacy: Tools load only when you open them, from this site’s own files. Your queries and files are processed locally.
workbench.smallScreen: This tool is easier to use on a larger screen. The visual builder and the chart options still work here.
guard.mixed-definitions: This result combines different case definitions{detail, select, other { ({detail})}}. Their numbers are not directly comparable.
guard.mixed-sources: This result combines different sources{detail, select, other { ({detail})}}. They may count differently.
guard.incomplete-included: This result includes periods marked likely incomplete. Recent values will probably be revised upward.
guard.cross-disease: This result combines different diseases ({detail}). Their counts come from different surveillance systems and must not be compared in size.
sql.title: SQL console
sql.lead: Runs DuckDB in your browser against the published Parquet files. Each file a query uses is downloaded to your device and read there.
sql.builderHint: Each choice below rewrites the SQL in the editor, so you can see how the query is formed.
sql.comparable: Comparable series only (default definition and source)
sql.help: Press Ctrl or Command + Enter to run. Queries are read-only and run on your device.
sql.loadAndRun: Load SQL engine (about {size} MB) and run
sql.share: Put query in the address bar
sql.downloading: Downloading the SQL engine: {done} of {total} MB
sql.result: {n, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}} in {ms} ms
sql.exportNote: Exports include a provenance file with the sources, snapshot, licenses and the SQL that produced the result.
sample.series: COVID-19 in Brazil, with source links
sample.revised: Values that were revised after publication
sample.flags: Recent signal flags with their method
method.user_sql_query: Result of a SQL query you wrote or built, run in your browser on the published files.
method.pivot: Values were grouped and aggregated by the rows and columns you chose.
method.chart_builder: A chart built from the published data with the variables and marks you chose.
method.snapshot_diff: Values published in two snapshots were compared.
method.sum_selected_places: Values were added across the places you selected; a period is kept only when every selected place reported.
method.range_rate: Rates were added over the date range you selected.
pivot.title: Pivot table
pivot.lead: Group and cross-tabulate one disease’s published data. Click a row to chart it.
pivot.note: {rows} records after filters. Missing values are skipped, never counted as zero.
builder.title: Chart builder
builder.lead: Build a chart from one disease’s published data. Exports carry the same title, source, date and license lines as the site’s own charts.
builder.placesHelp: Three-letter ISO country codes separated by commas, for example KEN,ETH. Leave empty for all countries.
builder.load: Load the charting library and draw
builder.alt: Chart of {n} records; a table of the same values follows.
builder.table: Show the {n} records as a table
diff.title: Snapshot diff
diff.lead: Compare what this site published at two moments.
diff.oneSnapshot: Only one snapshot exists so far, so there is nothing to compare yet. Differences will appear as the site updates.
diff.count: {n, plural, =0 {No values differ} one {# value differs} other {# values differ}}
diff.resultTitle: Values that differ between snapshots {a} and {b}
overlay.title: Your own data
overlay.lead: Plot a CSV of your own, for example counts from a clinic or school, next to the official series.
overlay.localTitle: Your file stays on this device.
overlay.local: It is read and processed in your browser, is never uploaded, and is never mixed into downloads of official data.
overlay.drop: or drop a CSV file here
overlay.rows: {n, plural, one {# valid row} other {# valid rows}} read.
overlay.means: The dashed dark line is your own data. It is shown on the same axis only so the shapes can be compared; it was collected differently from the official series.
overlay.meansEmpty: Choose a CSV file to add your own line to this chart.
overlay.exportNote: Your data is labelled user-supplied and is left out of data downloads from this chart.
overlay.err.noDate: Choose which column holds the date.
overlay.err.noValue: Choose which column holds the value.
overlay.err.sameColumn: The date and value columns must be different.
overlay.err.tooManyRows: The file has more than 50,000 rows. Please use a smaller file.
overlay.err.noValidRows: No rows had both a readable date and a number.
overlay.warn.ambiguousDates: Some dates could be read as day/month or month/day and were skipped. Use YYYY-MM-DD to be safe.
overlay.warn.skippedRows: {n, plural, one {# row was} other {# rows were}} skipped because the date or value could not be read.
mapsel.title: Map selection
mapsel.lead: Pick countries or draw a region to build two groups, then compare them.
mapsel.hint: Click countries to add or remove them from the active group, or draw a region to add every country whose centre lies inside it.
mapsel.means: Each line adds up the group’s countries and divides by their combined population. A period is shown only when every country in the group reported, so the groups are not made to look smaller by missing reports.
linked.title: Linked views
linked.lead: Drag across the chart to choose dates and click countries on the map. The map, table and event list all use the same selection.
linked.brush: Drag to choose a date range
linked.brushHint: The shaded band is the selected range.
nb.title: Notebooks
nb.lead: Starter notebooks load the site’s data, reproduce the main charts and signal flags, and show how to load a specific snapshot.
nb.liteMissing: The in-browser Python environment (JupyterLite) is not installed on this deployment. You can still download the notebooks and run them locally.
nb.webrMissing: The in-browser R runtime (webR) is not installed on this deployment. You can still download the notebooks and run them locally.
nb.local: Notebooks run entirely on your device. Nothing is sent to a server.
nb.rCode: R code (base R; edit and run)
